title.zh: 卷七十一 唐書47: 列傳23 馬郁 司空頲 曹廷隱 蕭希甫 藥縱之 賈馥 馬縞 羅貫 淳于晏 張格 許寂 周玄豹
title.en: Volume 71 Book of Later Tang 47: Biographies 23: Ma Yu, Si Kongting, Cao Tingyin, Xiao Xifu, Yao Zongzhi, Jia Fu, Ma Gao, Luo Guan, Chun Yuyan, Zhang Ge, Xu Ji, Zhou Xuanbao
title.raw: 卷七十一 唐書47: 列傳23 馬郁 司空頲 曹廷隱 蕭希甫 藥縱之 賈馥 馬縞 羅貫 淳于晏 張格 許寂 周玄豹 Volume 71 Book of Later Tang 47: Biographies 23: Ma Yu, Si Kongting, Cao Tingyin, Xiao Xifu, Yao Zongzhi, Jia Fu, Ma Gao, Luo Guan, Chun Yuyan, Zhang Ge, Xu Ji, Zhou Xuanbao

sentences.zh: 馬郁，其先范陽人。

translations.literal: Ma Yu—his ancestors were from Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yu came from a Fanyang family.

sentences.zh: 郁少警悟，有俊才智數，言辯縱橫，下筆成文。

translations.literal: As a youth Yu was alert and perceptive; he possessed outstanding talent and clever calculation, spoke with fluent and forceful eloquence, and produced compositions the moment he set brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick-witted and gifted with rare talent and resourcefulness; his speech was bold and fluent, and essays flowed from his brush as if unbidden.

sentences.zh: 乾寧末，為幽州府刀筆小吏。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianning era he served as a minor clerk handling documents in the Youzhou prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Qianning he was a low-ranking clerical officer in the Youzhou government.

sentences.zh: 李匡威為王鎔所殺，鎔書報其弟匡儔。

translations.literal: Li Kuangwei was killed by Wang Rong, and Rong wrote a letter informing his brother Kuangchou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Kuangwei was killed by Wang Rong, Rong sent a written report to Kuangchou, his brother.

sentences.zh: 匡儔遣使於鎔，問謀亂本末，幕客為書，多不如旨。

translations.literal: Kuangchou dispatched an envoy to Rong to inquire into the beginning and end of the plotting and rebellion; staff members drafted letters, but most failed to satisfy his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou sent a messenger to Rong to ask how the conspiracy had unfolded; several secretaries drafted replies, yet most missed what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 郁時直記室，即起草，為之條列事狀，雲可疑者十，詞理俊贍，以此知名。

translations.literal: At that time Yu was on duty in the secretariat; he immediately drafted a document, itemizing the facts of the case and citing ten points that seemed suspicious—the language was polished and ample, and he became famous for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, then serving in the records office, promptly drafted a memorial laying out the circumstances and ten suspicious points in elegant, forceful prose, and with that made his name.

sentences.zh: 嘗聘王鎔於鎮州，官妓有轉轉者，美麗善歌舞，因宴席，郁累挑之。

translations.literal: Once when he was visiting Wang Rong at Zhenzhou on a diplomatic mission, there was a government entertainer named Zhuanzhuan who was beautiful and skilled in song and dance; at a banquet Yu repeatedly flirted with her.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to Wang Rong at Zhenzhou he took notice of an official courtesan named Zhuanzhuan, renowned for her beauty and dancing; during the feast Yu kept pressing his attentions on her.

sentences.zh: 幕客張澤亦以文章名，謂郁曰：「子能座上成賦，可以此妓奉酬。」

translations.literal: The staff member Zhang Ze, who was also famed for his writing, said to Yu: "If you can compose a fu at the table, you may have this entertainer as your reward."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ze, another celebrated writer on the staff, challenged him: "Compose a fu here at the banquet, and the girl is yours."

sentences.zh: 郁抽筆操紙，即時成賦，擁妓而去。

translations.literal: Yu drew out his brush, took up paper, immediately completed the fu, and left embracing the entertainer.
translations.idiomatic: Yu seized brush and paper, finished the piece on the spot, and walked off with the girl in his arms.

sentences.zh: 郁在武皇幕，累官至檢校司空、秘書監。

translations.literal: While Yu served on Emperor Wu's staff, he rose in successive posts to Acting Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: In Li Keyong's service he rose through the ranks to honorary Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 武皇與莊宗禮遇俱厚，給賜優異。

translations.literal: Both Emperor Wu and Emperor Zhuangzong treated him with generous courtesy and gave him outstanding gifts and allowances.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong and his son Zhuangzong both honored him richly and showered him with exceptional rewards.

sentences.zh: 監軍張承業，本朝舊人，權貴任事，人士脅肩低首候之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Zhang Chengye was an elder of the founding house, wielded power as a favored official, and men of rank hunched their shoulders and bowed their heads waiting on him.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising commissioner Zhang Chengye, a veteran of the founding court, held real power; officials shrank before him and waited on him with bowed heads.

sentences.zh: 郁以滑稽侮狎，其往如歸，有時直造臥內。

translations.literal: Yu treated him with witty mockery and familiar disrespect; his visits were like returning home, and sometimes he went straight into the sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yu treated him with jesting familiarity, coming and going as freely as at home and sometimes walking straight into his bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 每賓僚宴集，承業出珍果陳列於前，食之必盡。

translations.literal: Whenever guests and colleagues feasted together, Chengye set out rare fruits before them, and Yu invariably ate every one.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet Chengye put out choice fruit before the guests, and Yu always ate every piece.

sentences.zh: 承業私戒主膳者曰：「他日馬監至，唯以乾藕子置前而已。」

translations.literal: Chengye privately warned the chief caterer: "When Director Ma comes another day, place only dried lotus seed before him."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye quietly told the head cook, "When Director Ma comes again, he should be served nothing but dried lotus seeds."

sentences.zh: 郁至，窺其不可啖；

translations.literal: When Yu arrived, he saw that they could not be eaten;
translations.idiomatic: When Yu arrived he saw they were inedible;

sentences.zh: 異日，靴中出一鐵楇，碎而食之。

translations.literal: On another day he pulled an iron pestle from his boot, broke it into pieces, and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: On another visit he produced an iron pestle from his boot, broke it into bits, and ate it.

sentences.zh: 承業大笑曰：「為公設異饌，勿敗餘食案。」

translations.literal: Chengye laughed loudly and said: "A special dish has been set out for you—do not ruin my remaining spread of food."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye roared with laughter: "This is a special feast just for you—please don't spoil the rest of my table."

sentences.zh: 其俊率如此。

translations.literal: His wit and boldness were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the measure of his wit and audacity.

sentences.zh: 郁在莊宗幕，寄寓他土，年老思鄉，每對莊宗欷歔，言家在范陽，乞骸歸國，以葬舊山。

translations.literal: While Yu was on Zhuangzong's staff, living as a guest in a foreign land, he grew old longing for home; whenever he faced Zhuangzong he would sigh with emotion, saying his family was in Fanyang and begging to return home in old age to be buried on his native hills.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong, far from home and advanced in years, he often wept before the throne, pleading to return to Fanyang to die and be buried among his ancestral hills.

sentences.zh: 莊宗謂之曰：「自卿去國已來，同舍孰在？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said to him: "Since you left your country, which of your old companions still remain there?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong told him, "Since you left your homeland, who among your old companions still survives there?

sentences.zh: 守光尚不能容父，能容卿乎！

translations.literal: Shouguang could not even bear his own father—how could he bear you!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang could not spare even his own father—do you think he would spare you?!

sentences.zh: 孤不惜卿行，但卿不得死爾。」

translations.literal: I do not begrudge you the journey, but you must not die."
translations.idiomatic: I would not withhold your leave, but you must not go home to die."

sentences.zh: 郁既無歸路，衷懷嗚咽，竟卒於太原。

translations.literal: Yu had no way to return; his heart choked with sobs, and he finally died at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: With no road home, his grief finally consumed him, and he died at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 司空頲，貝州人。

translations.literal: Si Kongting was a man of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Si Kongting came from Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 唐僖宗時，舉進士不中，屬天子播遷，三輔大亂，乃還鄉里。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xizong of Tang he took the jinshi examination but failed; as the Son of Heaven wandered in exile and the Three Metropolitan Regions fell into great disorder, he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong he failed the jinshi examinations; when the court fled the capital and the central plain collapsed into chaos, he went home.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威為節度副大使，頲以所業幹之，幕客公乘億為延譽，羅宏信署為府參軍，辟館驛巡官。

translations.literal: When Luo Shaowei was vice military commissioner, Ting presented his accomplishments to him; the staff member Gongcheng Yi spoke on his behalf, and Luo Hongxin appointed him a staff adjutant and commissioned him as post-station inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He sought patronage from Luo Shaowei, vice commissioner of the circuit; the staff member Gongcheng Yi vouched for him, and Luo Hongxin made him a staff adjutant and post-station inspector.

sentences.zh: 張彥之亂，命判官王正言草奏，正言素不能文，不能下筆，彥怒詬曰：「鈍漢乃辱我！」

translations.literal: During Zhang Yan's rebellion, he ordered the secretary Wang Zhengyan to draft the memorial; Zhengyan had never been able to write and could not set brush to paper; Yan angrily cursed him: "You dull-witted Han—how dare you shame me!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yan rebelled he ordered his aide Wang Zhengyan to draft a memorial, but Wang, who had never mastered prose, could not write a word; Zhang Yan thundered, "You blockheaded oaf—how dare you disgrace me!"

sentences.zh: 推之下榻。

translations.literal: He pushed him off the couch.
translations.idiomatic: He shoved him off the couch.

sentences.zh: 問孰可草奏者，有言頲，羅王時書記，乃馳騎召之。

translations.literal: He asked who could draft the memorial; someone said Ting, who had once been secretary to the Luo princes, and they galloped off on horseback to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Asked who could write the memorial, someone named Ting, formerly secretary to the Luo princes, and riders were sent at once to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 頲揮筆成文，詆斥梁君臣，彥甚喜，為判官。

translations.literal: Ting swept his brush and completed the text, denouncing the Liang ruler and ministers; Yan was greatly pleased and made him secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Ting wrote at speed, the draft lashing out at Liang sovereign and ministers; Zhang Yan was delighted and kept him as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 及張彥復脅賀德倫降於唐，德倫遣頲先奉狀太原。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yan again coerced He Delun to surrender to Tang, Delun sent Ting first to present the submission at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yan once more forced He Delun to surrender to Tang, Delun sent Ting ahead to Taiyuan with the formal submission.

sentences.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》載其狀詞云：屈原哀郢，本非怨望之人；

translations.literal: (The 《Beimeng Suoyan》 records that his petition read: Qu Yuan mourning Ying was never a man of resentful ambition;
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Beimeng Suoyan》, the memorial read: Qu Yuan grieving for Ying was no man nursing resentment;

sentences.zh: 樂毅歸燕，且異傾邪之行。）〉

translations.literal: Le Yi returning to Yan was still unlike a perverse and devious course.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Le Yi returning to Yan was still no act of treacherous defection.)〉

sentences.zh: 莊宗仍以頲為判官，後以頲權軍府事。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong still retained Ting as secretary, and later put him in charge of military headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong kept him as secretary and later entrusted him with authority over the military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 頲有侄在梁，遣家奴以書召之，都虞候張裕擒其家奴，以謂通於梁，遂見殺。

translations.literal: Ting had a nephew in Liang; he sent a household slave with a letter to summon him; the chief military inspector Zhang Yu seized the slave, charging that he was in communication with Liang, and Ting was therefore killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he sent a household slave with a letter to summon a nephew serving in Liang, Chief Inspector Zhang Yu seized the slave on suspicion of treasonous contact, and Ting was put to death.

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：晉王責頲曰：「自吾得魏博，庶事悉以委公，公何得見欺如是，獨不可先相示耶！」

translations.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》: The Prince of Jin rebuked Ting, saying, "Since I gained Weibo I have entrusted you with all affairs—how could you deceive me in this way? Could you not have informed me first!"
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 records that the Prince of Jin rebuked him: "Since I took Weibo I have entrusted you with everything—how could you deceive me like this? Could you not have told me first?!"

sentences.zh: 揖令歸第，是日族誅於軍門。）〉

translations.literal: He bowed him off to his residence, and that same day his entire clan was executed at the army gate.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed him to his quarters, and that same day Ting and his whole clan were executed at the army gate.)〉

sentences.zh: 曹廷隱，魏州人也，為本州典謁虞候。

translations.literal: Cao Tingyin was a man of Weizhou and served as reception officer and military inspector of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Tingyin, a native of Weizhou, served as reception officer and military inspector for that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賀德倫使西迎莊宗於晉陽，莊宗既得鄴城，擢為馬步都虞候，以其稱職，自是遷拜日隆。

translations.literal: He Delun sent him west to welcome Zhuangzong at Jinyang; once Zhuangzong had taken Yecheng, he promoted him to chief inspector of cavalry and infantry, and because he performed his duties well, his promotions thereafter grew ever more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: When He Delun sent him west to welcome Zhuangzong at Jinyang, Zhuangzong, after taking Yecheng, made him chief inspector of horse and foot; his capable service brought ever higher appointments thereafter.

sentences.zh: 天成初，除齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era he was appointed defense commissioner of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng era he was appointed defense commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 下車嚴整，頗有清白之譽。

translations.literal: On taking office he was strict and orderly and enjoyed a considerable reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he took office he ran a tight administration and earned a reputation for clean dealing.

sentences.zh: 時有孔目吏範弼者，為人剛愎，視廷隱蔑如也。

translations.literal: At the time there was a chief clerk named Fan Bi who was obstinate by nature and looked on Tingyin with utter contempt.
translations.idiomatic: A chief clerk named Fan Bi, stubborn and overbearing, treated Tingyin with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 弼監軍廩，鬻空乏以取貲；

translations.literal: Bi supervised the army granary and sold empty stores to take profit;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bi oversaw the army granary and sold off empty storehouses for cash;

sentences.zh: 又私貨官鹽，廷隱按之，遂奏其事。

translations.literal: he also trafficked in official salt on his own account; Tingyin investigated him and memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: he also trafficked illicitly in government salt; Tingyin investigated and reported him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 弼家人訴於執政，並下御史府劾之。

translations.literal: Bi's family appealed to the chief ministers, and both cases were sent down to the Censorate for impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's family appealed to the chief ministers, and both men were referred to the Censorate for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 弼雖伏法，廷隱以所奏不實，並流永州，續敕賜自盡，時人冤之。

translations.literal: Although Bi was executed by law, Tingyin was also banished to Yongzhou because his memorial was deemed untrue; a further edict ordered him to take his own life, and people of the time considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bi was executed, but Tingyin was exiled to Yongzhou as well when his charges were ruled unfounded; a later edict ordered him to commit suicide, and contemporaries regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 蕭希甫，宋州人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Xifu was a man of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xifu came from Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士，為梁開封尹袁象先書記。

translations.literal: In youth he took the jinshi examination and served as secretary to Yuan Xiangxian, Liang's prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he passed the jinshi examination and became secretary to Yuan Xiangxian, prefect of Kaifeng under Liang.

sentences.zh: 象先為青州節度使，以希甫為巡官，希甫不樂。

translations.literal: When Xiangxian became military commissioner of Qingzhou, he appointed Xifu as touring officer, but Xifu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangxian became military commissioner of Qingzhou he made Xifu a touring officer, a post Xifu disliked.

sentences.zh: 乃棄其母妻，變姓名，亡之鎮州，自稱青州掌書記，進謁王鎔。

translations.literal: He then abandoned his mother and wife, changed his name, fled to Zhenzhou, called himself chief secretary of Qingzhou, and presented himself to Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned his mother and wife, changed his name, fled to Zhenzhou, presented himself to Wang Rong as chief secretary of Qingzhou, and sought an audience.

sentences.zh: 鎔以希甫為參軍，尤不樂，居歲餘，又亡之易州，削髮為僧，居百丈山。

translations.literal: Rong made Xifu a staff adjutant, which pleased him even less; after more than a year he fled again to Yizhou, shaved his head, became a monk, and lived on Mount Baizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong appointed him a staff adjutant, which he liked even less; after a year he fled to Yizhou, took the tonsure, and lived as a monk on Mount Baizhang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗將建國，置百官，李紹宏薦為魏州推官。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was about to found the state and appoint the full bureaucracy, Li Shaohong recommended him as investigating officer of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhuangzong prepared to found his dynasty and fill the bureaucracy, Li Shaohong recommended him as investigating officer at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 同光初，有詔定內宴儀，問希甫樞密使得坐否，希甫以為不可。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era an edict was issued to fix the protocol for inner banquets; Xifu was asked whether the commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs might be seated, and he said it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongguang era, when court protocol for inner banquets was being set, he was asked whether the commissioner of military affairs should have a seat; Xifu said no.

sentences.zh: 樞密使張居翰聞之怒，謂希甫曰：「老夫曆事三朝天子，見內宴數百，子本田舍兒，安知宮禁事！」

translations.literal: The commissioner Zhang Juhan heard this and grew angry; he said to Xifu: "This old man has served three dynasties of Son of Heaven and witnessed hundreds of inner banquets—you, a rustic farm boy, what do you know of palace regulations!"
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Zhang Juhan flew into a rage: "I have served three emperors and attended hundreds of inner banquets—you're a country bumpkin; what do you know of palace protocol!"

sentences.zh: 希甫不能對。

translations.literal: Xifu could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu had no answer.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗欲以希甫知制誥，宰相豆盧革等附居翰，共排斥之，以為駕部郎中。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhuangzong had wished to make Xifu drafter of edicts; the chief ministers Dou Luge and others sided with Zhang Juhan and jointly pushed him aside, appointing him director in the Department of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had wanted to make him a drafter of edicts, but Chief Ministers Doulu Ge and others, siding with Zhang Juhan, blocked him and gave him only a post as director in the Transport Department.

sentences.zh: 希甫失誌，尤怏怏。

translations.literal: Xifu lost his ambition and was especially resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, he grew especially bitter.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁室，遣希甫宣慰青、齊，希甫始知其母已死，妻袁氏亦改嫁。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed the Liang house, he sent Xifu to announce consolation in Qing and Qi; only then did Xifu learn that his mother had died and that his wife, the Yuan clan, had remarried.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he sent Xifu to console Qing and Qi; only then did he learn his mother was dead and his wife of the Yuan clan had remarried.

sentences.zh: 希甫乃發哀服喪，居於魏州。

translations.literal: Xifu then put on mourning garb and observed the funeral rites, residing at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He donned mourning and observed the rites while living at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 人有引漢李陵書以譏之曰：「老母終堂，生妻去室。」

translations.literal: Someone quoted Li Ling's letter from Han to mock him, saying: "An aged mother reached her end in the hall; a living wife left the chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Someone mocked him with a line from Li Ling's letter to the Han: "His old mother died at home; his living wife abandoned their house."

sentences.zh: 天成初，欲召為諫議，豆盧革、韋說沮之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era he was to be summoned as remonstrating censor, but Dou Luge and Wei Shuo obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng era he was to be recalled as remonstrating censor, but Dou Luge and Wei Shuo blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 明宗卒以希甫為諫議大夫，復為匭函使。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong finally made Xifu Remonstrating Grand Master and again appointed him commissioner of the suggestion box.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong at last made him Remonstrating Grand Master and restored him as commissioner of the suggestion box.

sentences.zh: 其後革、說為安重誨所惡，希甫希旨，誣奏革縱田客殺人，而說與鄰人爭井，井有寶貨。

translations.literal: Later, when Luge and Shuo were hated by An Chonghui, Xifu curried favor and falsely memorialized that Luge had allowed his tenant farmers to kill people, and that Shuo had quarreled with a neighbor over a well said to contain treasure.
translations.idiomatic: When Luge and Shuo later fell afoul of An Chonghui, Xifu curried favor with false charges that Luge had let tenant farmers commit murder and that Shuo had fought a neighbor over a treasure-filled well.

sentences.zh: 有司推勘井中，惟破釜而已，革、說卒皆貶死。

translations.literal: The authorities investigated the well and found only a broken cauldron; Luge and Shuo were finally demoted and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Officials searched the well and found only a broken pot; Luge and Shuo were demoted and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 希甫拜左散騎常侍，躁進尤甚，引告變人李筠夜扣內門，通變書云：「修堤兵士，欲取郊天日舉火為叛。」

translations.literal: Xifu was appointed Left Regular Attendant and grew ever more frantic in his advancement; he brought in an informer named Li Yun, who knocked on the inner gate at night and submitted a report of treason, saying: "Soldiers repairing the dikes plan to raise fire in rebellion on the day of the suburban sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Regular Attendant, he grew ever more reckless; he brought in an informer, Li Yun, who knocked at the inner gate by night with a report that "dike-repair soldiers meant to rebel by fire on the day of the suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 安重誨不信之。

translations.literal: An Chonghui did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 斬告變者，軍人訴屈，請希甫啖之。

translations.literal: The informer was beheaded; the soldiers complained of injustice and asked that Xifu be eaten alive.
translations.idiomatic: The informer was executed; the soldiers protested their wrong and clamored to have Xifu torn apart.

sentences.zh: 既而詔曰：「左散騎常侍、集賢殿學士判院事蕭希甫，身處班行，職非警察，輒引凶狂之輩，上陳誣骫之詞，逼近郊禋，扇搖軍眾。

translations.literal: Soon an edict said: "Xiao Xifu, Left Regular Attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the institute—though he stands in the court ranks, policing is not his office—yet he rashly introduced violent and reckless men and submitted deceitful and crooked words, approaching the suburban sacrifice and inciting the army masses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Xiao Xifu, Left Regular Attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies—though he stands in court ranks, policing is not his charge—yet he introduced violent men and submitted deceitful charges, stirring the troops on the eve of the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 李筠既當誅戮，希甫寧免謫遷，可貶嵐州司戶參軍，仍馳驛發遣。」

translations.literal: Since Li Yun deserved execution, how could Xifu escape demotion and exile? He is demoted to registrar of Lanzhou and is to be dispatched post-haste by relay."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun was executed; Xifu could not escape demotion—to registrar of Lanzhou, dispatched at once by relay."

sentences.zh: 長興中，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: During the Changxing era he died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: He died in exile during the Changxing era.

sentences.zh: 子士明，仕周，終於邑宰。

translations.literal: His son Shiming served Zhou and ended his career as a district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiming served under the Zhou and ended his days as a district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 藥縱之，太原人，少為儒。

translations.literal: Yao Zongzhi was a man of Taiyuan. In youth he studied as a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zongzhi came from Taiyuan and in youth pursued Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 明宗刺代州，署為軍事衙推。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was military commissioner at Daizhou, he appointed him military affairs aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong served as military commissioner at Daizhou, he appointed Zongzhi military affairs aide.

sentences.zh: 從明宗鎮邢州，為掌書記，曆天平、宣武兩鎮節度副使。

translations.literal: Following Mingzong when he governed Xingzhou, he served as chief secretary and passed through vice military commissioner at the Tianping and Xuanwu circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Mingzong to Xingzhou as chief secretary and later served as vice military commissioner at Tianping and Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 明宗鎮常山，被病不從。

translations.literal: When Mingzong governed Changshan, Zongzhi fell ill and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong governed Changshan, illness kept Zongzhi from accompanying him.

sentences.zh: 及即位，縱之見於洛邑，安重誨怒其觀望，久無所授。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Zongzhi appeared at Luoyang; An Chonghui was angered by his hedging and long withheld any appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong took the throne, Zongzhi came to Luoyang; An Chonghui resented his fence-sitting and long gave him no post.

sentences.zh: 明宗曰：「德勝用兵時，縱之饑寒相伴，不離我左右。

translations.literal: Mingzong said: "When I was campaigning at Desheng, Zongzhi shared hunger and cold with me and never left my side.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "When I was campaigning at Desheng, Zongzhi shared hunger and cold with me and never left my side.

sentences.zh: 今有天下，何人不富貴，何為獨棄縱之！」

translations.literal: Now that I have the realm, who would not be enriched—why abandon Zongzhi alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have the realm, who would not prosper—why abandon Zongzhi alone!"

sentences.zh: 浹旬，授磁州刺史。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was appointed prefect of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was appointed prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，自戶部侍郎遷吏部侍郎，銓總之法，惘然莫知。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred from Vice Minister of Revenue to Vice Minister of Personnel, but the methods of evaluation and selection were beyond his understanding.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he rose from Vice Minister of Revenue to Vice Minister of Personnel, yet he was at a loss over the methods of evaluation and selection.

sentences.zh: 長興初，為曹州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in the Changxing era he was made prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing era he was appointed prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年九月，以疾受代而卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Qingtai he was relieved because of illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Qingtai 1 he was relieved for illness and died.

sentences.zh: 賈馥，故鎮州節度使王鎔判官也。

translations.literal: Jia Fu had been secretary to Wang Rong, former military commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Fu had served as secretary to Wang Rong, the former military commissioner of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 家聚書三千卷，手自刊校。

translations.literal: His household collected three thousand scrolls of books, which he personally collated and proofread.
translations.idiomatic: His family library held three thousand scrolls, which he collated and proofread with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 張文禮殺王鎔，時莊宗未即尊位，文禮遣馥至鄴都勸進，因留鄴下，棲遲郵舍。

translations.literal: When Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong, Zhuangzong had not yet taken the throne; Wenli sent Fu to Yedu to urge his accession, and Fu remained below Yedu, lingering at the post station.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong, while Zhuangzong had not yet taken the throne, Wenli sent Fu to Yedu to urge his accession; Fu stayed on there, lodging at the post station.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，授鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he appointed Fu Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong ascended the throne he appointed Fu Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 後以鴻臚卿致仕，復歸鎮州，結茅於別墅，自課兒孫耕牧為事。

translations.literal: Later he retired as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, returned to Zhenzhou, built a thatched dwelling at his country estate, and set his sons and grandsons to farming and herding as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, returned to Zhenzhou, built a thatched cottage on his estate, and taught his sons and grandsons to farm and herd.

sentences.zh: 馥初累為鎮、冀屬邑令，所蒞有能政，性恬澹，與物無競，乃鎮州士人之秀者也。

translations.literal: Fu had repeatedly served as magistrate of subordinate counties in Zhen and Ji; wherever he governed he showed capable administration; by nature he was tranquil and uncontentious, and he was among the finest gentlemen of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had served repeatedly as magistrate in counties under Zhen and Ji, governing capably wherever he went; tranquil by nature and free of worldly striving, he was counted among the finest scholars of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 馬縞，少嗜學儒，以明經及第，登拔萃之科。

translations.literal: Ma Gao in youth loved Confucian learning; he passed the Classics examination and also entered through the Outstanding Selections category.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gao loved Confucian learning from youth; he passed the Classics examination and also gained entry through the Outstanding Selections category.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為太常修撰，累曆尚書郎，參知禮院事，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He served Liang as compiler in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, rose through successive posts as Secretariat director, took part in managing the Bureau of Rites, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as compiler in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, rose through Secretariat posts, helped manage the Bureau of Rites, and became Vice Director of that court.

sentences.zh: 梁代諸王納嬪，公主下嫁，皆於宮殿門庭行揖讓之禮，縞以為非禮，上疏止之，物議以為然。

translations.literal: When Liang princes took brides and princesses married down, bowing and yielding ceremonies were all performed in the palace gates and courtyards; Gao held this uncanonical and memorialized to stop it, and public opinion agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang princes took brides and princesses married down, bowing and yielding rites were performed in the palace gates and courtyards; Gao held this improper and memorialized to stop it, and public opinion agreed.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: text is missing below.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: the text below is missing.)〉

sentences.zh: 長興四年，為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing he became Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 縞時年已八十，及為國子祭酒，八十餘矣，形氣不衰。

translations.literal: Gao was already eighty; when he became Rector of the Imperial University he was over eighty, yet his form and vigor did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: He was already eighty when appointed Rector of the Imperial University, and past eighty by then, yet his bearing and vigor had not faded.

sentences.zh: 於事多遺忘，言元稹不應進士，以父元魯山名進故也，多如此類。

translations.literal: In affairs he often forgot things; he said Yuan Zhen should not have taken the jinshi examination because his father Yuan Lushan had entered through the name Jin—many errors of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He often forgot things; he claimed Yuan Zhen should never have taken the jinshi because his father Yuan Lushan had entered through the name Jin—errors of that sort were common with him.

sentences.zh: 又上疏：「古者無嫂叔服，文皇創意，以兄弟之親，不宜無服，乃議服小功。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In antiquity there was no mourning for sister-in-law and brother-in-law; Emperor Wen innovated, holding that because of the closeness between brothers there should not be no mourning, and so lesser merit mourning was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "In antiquity there was no mourning dress for relations between brother's wife and husband's brother; Emperor Wen innovated, arguing that such close kin among brothers should not go unmourned, and lesser merit mourning was adopted.

sentences.zh: 今令文省服制條為兄弟之妻大功，不知何人議改，而置於令文。」

translations.literal: Now the statutes in the Code Office list great merit mourning for a brother's wife—I do not know who proposed this change, yet it was placed in the statutory text."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the current statutes prescribe great merit mourning for a brother's wife—I do not know who changed it, but it stands in the code."

sentences.zh: 諸博士駁云：「律令，國之大經。

translations.literal: The erudites rebutted, saying: "Statutes and ordinances are the great warp of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The erudites rebutted: "Statutes and ordinances are the great foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 馬縞知禮院時，不曾論定，今遽上疏駁令式，罪人也。」

translations.literal: When Ma Gao managed the Bureau of Rites he never discussed and settled this; now he rashly memorializes to rebut the statutes and forms—he is a criminal."
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Gao managed the Bureau of Rites he never raised this; now he rashly memorializes against the statutes—he is guilty of a crime."

sentences.zh: 羅貫，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Luo Guan—his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guan was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，累曆台省官，自禮部員外郎為河南令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through successive posts in the central ministries, advancing from Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites to magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he rose through central ministries from Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites to magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 貫為人強直，正身奉法，不避權豪。

translations.literal: Guan was forceful and upright by nature; he kept his person correct and upheld the law, never shunning the powerful and great.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was forceful and upright, held himself to the law, and never shrank from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 時宦官伶人用事，凡請托於貫者，其書盈閣，一無所報，皆以示郭崇韜，因奏其事，由是左右每言貫之失。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs and actor-favorites held power; every letter requesting favors sent to Guan filled his office, yet he answered none and showed them all to Guo Chongtao, who memorialized the matter; from this the emperor's intimates constantly spoke of Guan's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and actor-favorites held power; pleas to Guan filled his office, yet he answered none and showed them all to Guo Chongtao, who reported them to the throne; from then on the emperor's intimates constantly denounced Guan.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁時張全義專製京畿，河南、洛陽僚佐，皆由其門下，事全義如廝仆。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Liang times Zhang Quanyi monopolized control of the capital region; the staff of Henan and Luoyang all came through his gate and served Quanyi like bond servants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang, Zhang Quanyi had monopolized the capital region; staff in Henan and Luoyang all entered through his patronage and served him like bond servants.

sentences.zh: 及貫授命，持本朝事體，奉全義稍慢，部民為府司庇護者，必奏正之。

translations.literal: When Guan received his appointment, he upheld the proper forms of the present dynasty, treated Quanyi with somewhat less deference, and whenever local people were sheltered by Quanyi's staff he would memorialize to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guan took office he upheld the proper forms of the new dynasty, treated Quanyi with less deference, and whenever locals were shielded by Quanyi's staff he reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 全義怒，因令女使告劉皇后從容白於莊宗，宦官又言其短，莊宗深怒之。

translations.literal: Quanyi grew angry and had a female attendant tell Empress Liu to speak gently to Zhuangzong on his behalf; the eunuchs also spoke of Guan's faults, and Zhuangzong was deeply enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi, furious, had a female attendant ask Empress Liu to speak to Zhuangzong on his behalf; the eunuchs added their complaints, and Zhuangzong grew deeply angry.

sentences.zh: 會莊宗幸壽安山陵，道路泥濘，莊宗訪其主者，宦官曰：「屬河南縣。」

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong visited the Shou'an imperial tombs, the roads were muddy; Zhuangzong asked who was responsible, and a eunuch said: "It falls under Henan County."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong visited the Shou'an tombs the roads were muddy; asked who was responsible, a eunuch said, "That is Henan County's charge."

sentences.zh: 促令召貫至，奏曰：「臣初不奉命，請詰稟命者。」

translations.literal: He urgently ordered Guan summoned; Guan memorialized, saying: "I did not at first receive the command—please interrogate whoever reported the order."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guan summoned at once; Guan replied, "I never received the order in the first place—question whoever reported it."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿之所部，反問他人，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your own jurisdiction—and you ask others? Why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is your jurisdiction—why are you asking someone else?"

sentences.zh: 命下府獄，府吏榜笞，促令伏款。

translations.literal: He ordered him sent down to the prefectural prison; the clerks beat him with the cudgel and pressed him to confess.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the prefectural prison, beaten by the clerks, and pressed to confess.

sentences.zh: 翌日，傳詔殺之。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was transmitted ordering his execution.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜奏曰：「貫別無贓狀，橋道不修，法未當死。」

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao memorialized: "Guan has no other evidence of corruption; failure to repair bridges and roads does not warrant death under the law."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao argued, "Guan shows no other sign of corruption; neglected roads and bridges are not a capital offense."

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒曰：「母後靈駕將發，天子車輿往來，橋道不修，是誰之過也？」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong angrily said: "The late empress's spirit carriage is about to depart; the Son of Heaven's chariots come and go—whose fault is it that bridges and roads are not repaired?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raged, "The late empress's funeral procession is about to set out, and the emperor's carriages must pass—whose fault is it that the roads are ruined?"

sentences.zh: 崇韜奏曰：「貫縱有死罪，俟款狀上奏，所司議讞，以朝典行之，死當未晚。

translations.literal: Chongtao memorialized: "Even if Guan deserves death, wait until his confession is memorialized, let the responsible offices deliberate the sentence, and carry it out by court statute—death will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao urged, "Even if Guan deserves death, let him confess, let the proper offices judge, and execute him by statute—it is not yet too late to kill him.

sentences.zh: 今以萬乘之尊，怒一縣令，俾天下人言陛下使法不公矣！」

translations.literal: Now, with the dignity of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler, to rage at a county magistrate will make all under heaven say Your Majesty makes the law unjust!"
translations.idiomatic: For the ruler of an empire to vent his wrath on a county magistrate will make the realm say you pervert justice!"

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「既卿所愛，任卿裁決。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said: "Since he is the one you favor, I leave the decision to you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "Since he is your man, you decide."

sentences.zh: 因投袂入宮。

translations.literal: With that he flung his sleeve and entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: With that he flung his sleeve and stalked into the palace.

sentences.zh: 崇韜從而論列，莊宗自闔殿門，不得入。

translations.literal: Chongtao followed, arguing point by point; Zhuangzong himself closed the hall doors and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao followed, arguing each point; Zhuangzong shut the hall doors himself and could not get in.

sentences.zh: 即令伏法，曝屍於府門，冤痛之聲，聞於遠邇。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered execution; the corpse was exposed at the prefectural gate, and cries of injustice were heard far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was executed at once; his body was exposed at the prefectural gate, and cries of injustice rang far and wide.

sentences.zh: 淳於晏，

translations.literal: Chunyu Yan,
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Yan

sentences.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: text is missing below.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: the text below is missing.)〉

sentences.zh: 以明經登第，自霍彥威為小校，晏寄食於門下。

translations.literal: He passed the Classics examination; from the time Huo Yanwei was a junior officer, Yan lodged and ate at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: A Classics examination graduate, he had lived as a dependent in Huo Yanwei's household since Yanwei was a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 彥威嘗因兵敗，獨脫其身，左右莫有從者，惟晏杖劍從之，徒步草莽，自是彥威高其義，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Yanwei once escaped alone after a defeat in battle; none of his attendants followed, only Yan, sword in hand, followed him on foot through the wild grass; from this Yanwei esteemed his loyalty and they became very close.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after a defeat, Yanwei escaped alone with no attendants—only Yan followed on foot through the wilds, sword in hand; from then on Yanwei prized his loyalty and they grew very close.

sentences.zh: 及曆數鎮，皆為從事，軍府之事，至於私門，事無巨細，皆取決於晏；

translations.literal: When he served successively in several commands, Yan was always a staff officer; from military headquarters affairs down to private household matters, nothing great or small was decided without Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Through successive commands Yan served as staff officer; from military headquarters down to the private household, nothing great or small was decided without him;

sentences.zh: 雖為幕賓，有若家宰。

translations.literal: though a staff guest, he was like a household steward.
translations.idiomatic: though nominally a staff guest, he was like the master of the house.

sentences.zh: 爾後公侯門客，往往效之，時謂之「效淳」。

translations.literal: Afterward the retainers of dukes and marquises often imitated this, and the age called it "imitating Chun."
translations.idiomatic: Later retainers of great lords often imitated him, and the age spoke of "imitating Chun."

sentences.zh: 故彥威所至稱治，由晏之力也。

translations.literal: Thus wherever Yanwei went he was praised for good governance—this was through Yan's power.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yanwei went he was praised for good governance, and it was Yan's doing.

sentences.zh: 張格，字承之，故宰相浚之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ge, courtesy name Chengzhi, was the son of the former chief minister Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ge, styled Chengzhi, was the son of the former chief minister Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚為梁祖所忌，潛遣人害於長水。

translations.literal: Jun was hated by the Liang founder, who secretly sent men to kill him at Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was hated by the Liang founder, who secretly had him killed at Changshui.

sentences.zh: 格易姓名，流轉入蜀。

translations.literal: Ge changed his name and wandered into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Ge changed his name and made his way into Shu.

sentences.zh: 〈（《舊唐書·張浚傳》：永寧縣吏葉彥者，張氏待之素厚，告格曰：「相公之禍不可免，郎君宜自為計。」

translations.literal: (The Old Book of Tang, biography of Zhang Jun: Ye Yan, a clerk of Yongning County, whom the Zhang family had long treated well, told Ge: "The chief minister's disaster cannot be avoided—you, young master, should make your own plans."
translations.idiomatic: (The Old Book of Tang, biography of Zhang Jun: Ye Yan, a Yongning county clerk whom the Zhangs had long favored, told Ge, "Your father's doom cannot be avoided—you must save yourself."

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「留則並命，去或可免，冀存後嗣。」

translations.literal: Jun said: "If you stay we die together; if you go you may escape—I hope to preserve our descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "If you stay we die together; if you go you may live—I hope our line survives."

sentences.zh: 格拜辭而去，葉彥率義士三十人送渡漢江而旋。

translations.literal: Ge bowed in farewell and left; Ye Yan led thirty righteous men to escort him across the Han River and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ge took his leave; Ye Yan led thirty volunteers to see him across the Han River and then turned back.

sentences.zh: 格由荊江上峽入蜀。）〉

translations.literal: Ge entered Shu by way of the Jing River gorges.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Ge entered Shu through the Yangtze gorges.)〉

sentences.zh: 王建僭號，以格為宰相。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian usurped the title, he made Ge chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian declared himself emperor, he made Ge his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 格所生母，當浚之遇害，潛匿於民間，落發為尼，流浪於函、洛。

translations.literal: Ge's birth mother, when Jun met his death, hid among the people, shaved her head and became a nun, and wandered between Hangu and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was killed, Ge's mother went into hiding among the people, took the tonsure, and wandered between the Hangu Pass and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 王建聞之，潛使人迎之入蜀，賜紫，加號慈福大師。

translations.literal: Wang Jian heard of this and secretly sent men to welcome her into Shu, granted her the purple robe, and gave her the title Great Master Cifu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian heard of it and secretly had her brought to Shu, granted her the purple robe, and gave her the title Great Master Cifu.

sentences.zh: 及建卒，蜀人以格為山陵使，格有難色。

translations.literal: When Jian died, the people of Shu appointed Ge commissioner for the imperial tombs, and Ge showed a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian died, Shu made Ge commissioner for the imperial tombs, and Ge looked uneasy.

sentences.zh: 未幾得罪，出為茂州刺史，偽製責詞云：「送往辭命，不忠也；

translations.literal: Before long he offended and was sent out as prefect of Maozhou; a forged reprimand read: "Sent off yet declining the commission—this is disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell from favor and was sent out as prefect of Maozhou; a forged reprimand charged, "Sent on an errand yet refusing the commission—disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 喪母匿喪，非孝也。」

translations.literal: his mother's death concealed and mourning hidden—this is unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: concealing his mother's death and hiding mourning—unfilial."

sentences.zh: 王衍嗣偽位後數年，復用為宰相。

translations.literal: Several years after Wang Yan succeeded to the usurped throne, Ge was again employed as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after Wang Yan took the throne, he was again made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 同光末，蜀平，格至洛陽，

translations.literal: At the end of the Tongguang era Shu was pacified, and Ge came to Luoyang,
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell at the end of Tongguang, Ge came to Luoyang,

sentences.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：任圜攜格還洛，格感葉彥之惠，訪之，身已歿，厚恤其家。

translations.literal: (The Old Book of Tang: Ren Yuan brought Ge back to Luoyang; Ge, grateful for Ye Yan's kindness, sought him out, but he was already dead, and Ge generously provided for his family.
translations.idiomatic: (The Old Book of Tang: Ren Yuan brought Ge back to Luoyang; remembering Ye Yan's kindness, Ge sought him out, found him dead, and generously provided for his family.

sentences.zh: 又考張浚第三子仕吳，改名李儼，見《九國志》。）〉

translations.literal: It is also recorded that Zhang Jun's third son served Wu and changed his name to Li Yan, as seen in the Jiuguo Zhi.)〉
translations.idiomatic: It also records that Zhang Jun's third son served Wu under the name Li Yan, as noted in the Jiuguo Zhi.)〉

sentences.zh: 授太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The court made him Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 任圜愛其才，奏為三司副使，尋卒於位。

translations.literal: Ren Yuan admired his talent and memorialized to make him deputy commissioner of the Three Offices; he soon died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan admired his talent and had him made deputy commissioner of the Three Offices; he soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 格有文章，明吏事，時頗稱之。

translations.literal: Ge had literary talent and understood administrative affairs; his contemporaries spoke well of him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was a capable writer and administrator, and his contemporaries spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 許寂，字閑閑。

translations.literal: Xu Ji, courtesy name Xianxian.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji, styled Xianxian.

sentences.zh: 祖秘，名聞會稽。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mi was famed in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mi was renowned in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 寂少有山水之好，泛覽經史，窮三式，尤明《易》象。

translations.literal: Ji in youth loved mountains and waters; he read widely in the classics and histories, mastered the Three Styles, and was especially skilled in the imagery of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved landscape; he read widely in the classics and histories, mastered the Three Styles of divination, and was especially versed in the imagery of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》云：寂學《易》於晉徵君。）〉

translations.literal: (The Taiping Guangji says: Ji studied the Changes under the Jin Recluse.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Taiping Guangji records that Ji studied the Changes under the Jin Recluse.)〉

sentences.zh: 久棲四明山，不幹時譽。

translations.literal: He long dwelt on Mount Siming and did not seek the fame of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He lived long on Mount Siming and shunned worldly renown.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聞其名，征赴闕，召對於內殿。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong heard his name and summoned him to court, calling him to audience in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong heard of him, summoned him to court, and received him in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 會昭宗方與伶人調品篳篥，事訖，方命坐賜果，問《易》義。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhaozong was just tuning the pitch of the bili pipe with actor-favorites; when that was finished, he ordered Ji seated, granted fruit, and asked about the meaning of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong happened to be tuning a pipe with his actor-favorites; when they finished, he had Ji seated, gave him fruit, and questioned him on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 既退，寂謂人曰：「君淫在聲，不在政矣。

translations.literal: After he withdrew, Ji said to others: "The ruler's excess lies in sound, not in government.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving audience he told others, "The ruler's excess lies in music, not in government.

sentences.zh: 寂聞君人者，將昭德塞違，以臨照百官，百官或象之。

translations.literal: Ji had heard that a ruler should display virtue and block wrongdoing to oversee the hundred officials, and that the hundred officials would mirror him.
translations.idiomatic: He had heard that a ruler should display virtue and restrain wrongdoing to oversee his officials, and that officials would mirror him.

sentences.zh: 今不厭賤事，自求其工，君道替矣。」

translations.literal: Now he does not disdain base tasks but seeks his own skill in them—the way of rulership is in decline."
translations.idiomatic: Now he does not disdain petty tasks but pursues his own skill in them—the way of rulership is failing."

sentences.zh: 尋請還山，寓居於江陵，以茹芝絕粒，自適其性。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to return to the mountains, lodged at Jiangling, ate fungus and abstained from grain, and suited his own nature.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return to the mountains, settled at Jiangling, lived on fungus and abstained from grain, and followed his own inclinations.

sentences.zh: 天祐末，節度使趙匡凝昆季深禮遇之，師授保養之道。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianyou era the military commissioners Zhao Kuangning and his brothers treated him with deep courtesy and learned from him the ways of nurturing life.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianyou the Zhao brothers, military commissioners of the region, honored him deeply and studied the arts of nurturing life under him.

sentences.zh: 唐末，除諫官，不起，漢南謂之徵君。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang he was appointed remonstrating official but did not take office; south of the Han they called him the Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tang he was offered a remonstrating post but declined; south of the Han they called him the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 梁攻襄陽，匡凝兄弟棄鎮奔蜀，寂偕行。

translations.literal: When Liang attacked Xiangyang, the Kuangning brothers abandoned their command and fled to Shu, and Ji went with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang attacked Xiangyang, the Kuangning brothers abandoned their post and fled to Shu, and Ji went with them.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，蜀主王建待以師禮，位至蜀相。

translations.literal: After more than a year the Shu ruler Wang Jian treated him with the courtesy due a teacher, and he rose to chief minister of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Wang Jian of Shu treated him as a teacher and raised him to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 同光末，平蜀，與王衍俱從於東，授工部尚書致仕，卜居於洛。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang Shu was pacified; he followed Wang Yan east, was appointed Minister of Works and retired, and chose his dwelling at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell at the end of Tongguang he followed Wang Yan east, retired as Minister of Works, and settled at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時寂已年高，精彩猶健，衝漠寡言，時蜀語云「可怪可怪」，人莫知其際。

translations.literal: By then Ji was advanced in years, yet his spirit was still vigorous; he was remote and sparing of speech. A saying in Shu ran "strange, strange," and no one knew what he meant.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was old, yet still vigorous and remote, saying little. In Shu they said "how strange, how strange," and no one knew what he meant.

sentences.zh: 清泰三年六月卒，時年八十餘。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth month of the third year of Qingtai, at over eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of Qingtai 3, past eighty years old.

sentences.zh: 子孫位至省郎。

translations.literal: His descendants rose to Secretariat directors.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants rose to posts as Secretariat directors.

sentences.zh: 同光時，以方術著者，又有僧誠惠。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era, among those famed for occult arts, there was also the monk Chenghui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tongguang era another figure famed for occult arts was the monk Chenghui.

sentences.zh: 誠惠初於五台山出家，能修戒律，稱通皮、骨、肉三命，人初歸向，聲名漸遠，四方供饋，不遠千里而至者眾矣。

translations.literal: Chenghui first left home at Mount Wutai, could keep the precepts, and was said to penetrate the three fates of skin, bone, and flesh; people first turned to him, his fame gradually spread far, and offerings came from all directions—many came from more than a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui first took orders on Mount Wutai, kept the precepts strictly, and was said to master the three fates of skin, bone, and flesh; disciples gathered, his fame spread, and donors came from a thousand li and more.

sentences.zh: 自雲能役使毒龍，可致風雨，其徒號曰降龍大師。

translations.literal: He claimed he could command poisonous dragons and bring wind and rain; his disciples called him the Great Master Who Subdues Dragons.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he could command poisonous dragons and summon rain; his disciples called him the Dragon-Subduing Master.

sentences.zh: 京師旱，莊宗迎至洛下，親拜之，六宮參禮，士庶瞻仰，謂朝夕可致甘澤。

translations.literal: When the capital suffered drought, Zhuangzong welcomed him to Luoyang, bowed to him in person, the six palaces paid homage, and officials and commoners looked up to him, believing sweet moisture would come at any moment.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital suffered drought, Zhuangzong brought him to Luoyang, bowed to him in person, the inner court paid homage, and the people looked to him for rain at any moment.

sentences.zh: 禱祝數旬，略無征應。

translations.literal: After several tens of days of prayer there was scarcely any sign of response.
translations.idiomatic: After weeks of prayer there was no sign of rain.

sentences.zh: 或謂官以祈雨無驗，將加焚燎，誠惠懼而遁去。

translations.literal: Some said the authorities, because the rain prayer had failed, would burn him alive; Chenghui, afraid, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the authorities would burn him for failing to bring rain; Chenghui fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 及卒，賜號法雨大師，塔曰「慈雲之塔。」

translations.literal: When he died he was granted the title Great Master Fayu, and his stupa was called "Stupa of Kind Clouds."
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was given the title Great Master Fayu, and his stupa was named "Kind Clouds Stupa."

sentences.zh: 周元豹者，本燕人，世為從事。

translations.literal: Zhou Yuanbao was originally a man of Yan; for generations his family had served as staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yuanbao came from Yan; for generations his family had served as staff officers.

sentences.zh: 元豹少為僧，其師有知人之鑒，從遊十年餘，苦辛無憚，師知其可教，遂以袁、許之術授之。

translations.literal: Yuanbao in youth became a monk; his teacher had the discernment to know men; he followed him for more than ten years, toiling without complaint; the teacher knew he could be taught and therefore imparted to him the arts of Yuan and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yuanbao became a monk; his teacher, skilled at reading men, trained him for more than ten years of hard service and then taught him the physiognomy of Yuan Tian gang and Xu Fu.

sentences.zh: 大略狀人形貌，比諸龜魚禽獸，目視臆斷，鹹造其理。

translations.literal: In general he described people's forms and features, comparing them to turtles, fish, birds, and beasts, judging by sight and intuition, and always constructing a rationale.
translations.idiomatic: He compared people's features to turtles, fish, birds, and beasts, judged at a glance, and always found a rationale.

sentences.zh: 及還鄉，遂歸俗。

translations.literal: When he returned home he left the clergy.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home he returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 初，盧程寄褐遊燕，與同志二人謁焉。

translations.literal: Early on Lu Cheng, wearing plain robes while traveling in Yan, visited him with two like-minded companions.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Lu Cheng, traveling in Yan in plain robes, visited him with two companions.

sentences.zh: 元豹謂鄉人張殷袞曰：「適二君子，明年花發，俱為故人。

translations.literal: Yuanbao said to his townsman Zhang Yingun: "Those two gentlemen just now—when the flowers bloom next year they will both be departed friends.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao told his townsman Zhang Yingun, "Those two visitors—when the flowers bloom next year they will both be dead.

sentences.zh: 惟彼道士，他年甚貴。」

translations.literal: Only that Daoist will be very exalted in years to come."
translations.idiomatic: Only that Daoist will rise very high one day."

sentences.zh: 至來歲，二子果卒。

translations.literal: When the next year came, the two men indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the two men died as he had said.

sentences.zh: 又二十年，盧程登庸於鄴下。

translations.literal: Twenty years later Lu Cheng rose to high office at Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years on, Lu Cheng indeed reached high office at Yedu.

sentences.zh: 元豹歸晉陽，張承業信重之，言事數中。

translations.literal: Yuanbao returned to Jinyang; Zhang Chengye trusted and valued him, and his predictions often hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao returned to Jinyang, where Zhang Chengye trusted him and found his predictions often accurate.

sentences.zh: 承業俾明宗易衣列於諸校之下，以他人詐之，而元豹指明宗於末綴言曰：「骨法非內衙太保歟！」

translations.literal: Chengye had Mingzong change clothes and stand among the junior officers, substituting another man to deceive him, but Yuanbao pointed out Mingzong at the rear rank and said: "Is not this bone-structure that of the Inner Palace Grand Guardian!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye had Mingzong change clothes and stand among the junior officers, substituting another man to test him; Yuanbao pointed to Mingzong at the rear and said, "Isn't that the bone-structure of the Inner Palace Grand Guardian?!"

sentences.zh: 鹹伏其異。

translations.literal: All submitted to his uncanny skill.
translations.idiomatic: All were awed by his uncanny skill.

sentences.zh: 或問明宗之福壽，惟云末後為鎮州節度使，時明宗為內衙都校，才兼州牧而已。

translations.literal: When asked about Mingzong's fortune and lifespan, he only said that in the end he would be military commissioner of Zhenzhou; at the time Mingzong was chief inspector of the inner barracks, holding at most the concurrent post of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Mingzong's fortune, he said only that in the end he would be military commissioner of Zhenzhou—though Mingzong was then merely chief inspector of the inner barracks with a prefect's title.

sentences.zh: 昭懿皇后夏氏方侍巾櫛，偶忤旨，大為明宗檟楚。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaoyi of the Xia clan was then attending to Mingzong's toilet and comb; she once offended his will and was severely beaten by Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaoyi of the Xia clan, then attending Mingzong, once offended him and was beaten severely.

sentences.zh: 元豹見之曰：「此人有藩侯夫人之位，當生貴子。」

translations.literal: Yuanbao saw this and said: "This woman has the rank of a feudal lord's wife and will bear an exalted son."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao saw it and said, "This woman is destined to be a feudal lord's wife and will bear an exalted son."

sentences.zh: 明宗赫怒因解，後其言果驗。

translations.literal: Mingzong's fierce anger was thereby dispelled, and later his words proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong's rage cooled, and later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 太原判官司馬揆謁元豹，謂揆曰：「公五日之中，奉使萬里，未見回期。」

translations.literal: Sima Kui, secretary of Taiyuan, visited Yuanbao; Yuanbao told Kui: "Within five days you will go on a mission ten thousand li, with no date of return in sight."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Kui, secretary at Taiyuan, visited Yuanbao, who told him, "Within five days you will go on a mission ten thousand li away, with no return in sight."

sentences.zh: 揆數日後，因酒酣，為衣領扼之而卒。

translations.literal: Several days later, while drunk, Kui was strangled by his collar and died.
translations.idiomatic: Days later, drunk, Kui was strangled by his collar and died.

sentences.zh: 莊宗署元豹北京巡官。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong appointed Yuanbao touring officer of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong appointed him touring officer of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位之明年，一日，謂侍臣曰：「方士周元豹，昔曾言朕諸事有征，可詔北京津置赴闕。」

translations.literal: In the year after Mingzong took the throne, one day he said to his attendants: "The adept Zhou Yuanbao once spoke of many matters concerning me that were fulfilled—issue an edict to provide relay transport from the Northern Capital and summon him to court."
translations.idiomatic: The year after Mingzong took the throne he told his attendants, "The adept Zhou Yuanbao once predicted many things about me that came true—summon him from the Northern Capital to court."

sentences.zh: 趙鳳奏曰：「袁、許之事，元豹所長者，以陛下貴不可言，今既驗矣，餘無可問。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng memorialized: "The arts of Yuan and Xu are what Yuanbao excels at; he said Your Majesty's nobility was beyond words, and that has now been verified—there is nothing else to ask.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng objected, "Yuanbao excels at the arts of Yuan and Xu; he said Your Majesty's destiny was beyond words, and that has been proved—there is nothing left to ask.

sentences.zh: 若詔赴闕下，則奔競之徒，爭問吉凶，恐近於妖惑。」

translations.literal: If he is summoned to court, the scrambling crowd will vie to ask fortune and misfortune, and I fear this will verge on sorcerous delusion."
translations.idiomatic: If he comes to court, the scrambling crowd will pester him for omens, and that will verge on sorcery."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The summons was therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The summons was dropped.

sentences.zh: 令以金帛厚賜之，授光祿卿致仕。

translations.literal: He ordered that gold and silk be given generously, and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generous gifts of gold and silk and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness in retirement.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於太原，年八十餘。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at Taiyuan, aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after at Taiyuan, past eighty years old.
